visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md. No mockup ever existed for the blog post; this file exists so the class carries a taste receipt (SITE-31, 2026-09-09) and so ci:mockup-parity notices if the post loses a section.
competitiveTarget: A portal's neighborhood article: stock photo, listicle, no figure with a source. We publish a post whose every number carries its window and sample, a Questions block that becomes FAQPage, and the place page one tap away.
note: Created 2026-09-09 for SITE-31 (eleven community guides). The first mark, 52, was taken on the template as it stood; the receipt below is the SECOND mark, on the same evaluator model and the same rubric, after the class was rebuilt: a capped photographic masthead carrying the title, a byline row that carries Share, the post's own figures beside the prose with the sentence each one came from, the Questions block as disclosures, and every outbound citation wearing its host. The shots moved to one of the eleven guides, so shotsHash differs and the pair is recorded as a rebaseline with the prior mark kept.

tasteReview.evaluator: A separate evaluator run as its own Claude Code process from the lane's worktree (`claude -p --model sonnet --allowedTools Read`, prompt in the lane's scratchpad), given only the four shot paths, the rubric verbatim and TASTE.md's banned tells, told to read the PNGs and nothing else — no page code, no URL, no score to hit. Second of two rounds; the first, on the pre-fix capture, returned 63/70/67 (median 67) and its named defects (mobile breadcrumb wrapping onto a hanging separator, and a figure rail whose plain-language sentence sat under the numbers instead of with them) were fixed before this capture.

shotSpec.capture: scripts/take-route-shots.mjs against the lane's own next dev, device scale 1, palette-quantized. The route moved from the pre-SITE-31 exemplar to one of the eleven guides published 2026-09-09, so the class is now scored on a post built to its own spec.

tasteReview.beats: The evaluator's own words: loses to a magazine-style neighborhood feature (a Curbed / The Real Deal community deep-dive) on visual richness and inline data viz inside the body; beats a Redfin or Zillow neighborhood page on data honesty (explicit sample sizes, and it says plainly that there is no publishable asking price for the three homes on the market) and on having one coherent typographic identity instead of a generic template shell.
tasteReview.scoringNotes: Three independent scorings of the same four PNGs in one call: 74, 68, 77, median 74, spread 9 — inside the 5-13 spread this instrument has shown on other classes. No banned tell was found this round; the first mark had recorded "walls of text" against the same template.
tasteReview.topThree: What the evaluator says is still capping the number, in its order: 1) the article body carries no inline data encoding — every section is a heading and two paragraphs, and all the interaction lives in the rail; a chart inside a section needs a series the post does not carry, so it needs data work, not layout work. 2) the rail's cards all share one shape. 3) the H1 breaks the dollar figure across two lines in both viewports.

defects.finding: Every body section is heading plus two paragraphs of prose with zero inline data encoding; all interactivity lives in the sidebar rail, so the primary reading column is text-only and rewards no hover or tap of its own. Owner: app/blog/[slug]/_v3/article-view.ts. The honest fix is a series per section, which this post does not carry — it is a data question for a future node, not a layout one, and a drawn chart off a number the body does not hold would break CLAUDE.md section 0.

The stat cards repeat one identical shape down the rail — big serif number, question label, expand toggle — with no differentiation between a price, a pace and a count, so collapsed the rail reads as a plain KPI list. Owner: app/blog/[slug]/_v3/BlogArticleRail.client.tsx. Fix: give each figure kind its own mark (a currency, a duration and a count should not be the same object).

The dollar figure '$1,349,000' breaks across two lines in both the desktop and the mobile hero, which fights the single-figure-as-hero effect the rest of the page relies on. Owner: components/site/v3/V3Stage.tsx, whose headline is a plain string and so cannot carry a non-breaking span; fixing it is a change to that primitive, which another node owns this round.

At 375 the last visible figure card is cut by the fold with no affordance saying more figures continue below. Owner: app/blog/[slug]/_v3/blog-article.css. Fix: a count on the rail label, or a bottom rule that reads as continuing.

tasteReview.rebaselineReason: shotsHash is the key that differs: the prior mark's four PNGs were the pre-SITE-31 template rendered on /blog/sunriver-year-round-living-vs-vacation, and these four are the rebuilt class rendered on /blog/awbrey-glen-median-price-hoa-dues-2026, one of the eleven guides published 2026-09-09. evaluatorModel (claude-sonnet-5) and rubricVersion (v1-2026-09-08) are unchanged, so the two numbers are from the same instrument on different pixels. Stated plainly: the median ROSE, 52 to 74, on the same evaluatorModel and the same rubricVersion, over a rebuilt page and a new capture set.

contentFloor.note: No-regression floor (ci:route-content-floor). A build under any number here fails before the evaluator runs. Lower a number only by hand, in the same commit, with the reason.
